title: Write each workspace's urlKey to the registry when it is created or bound
description:
Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour). One PR.

Series: Step 1 of 3 (LIN-3394). Depends on: nothing. Next: step 2. The row shape below is a contract for steps 2 and 3.

## Why

LIN-3394 needs one durable record of "this urlKey belongs to this workspace id" before a unique index can exist. `workspaces` is meant to be it, but nothing writes it. This step fills it, one row per urlKey: no read switches to it, no index, no backfill. On 9 Oct production had no `workspaces` rows under the four Linear keys (LIN-3382).

## What is true now

* `WorkspaceStore` (lib/workspace-store.js:26) is built at server.js:642, passed to no route (comment :634-640). `createWorkspace` stores the whole workspace (:59); the registry row must not.
* Remove-then-re-add gives the same key and, for GitHub-fresh and held-new, a new random id (lib/github-install-flow.js:936, routes/held-connection.js:316; tests/unit/lin-3382-bind-arms.test.js:190-197).

## Done when

1. `WorkspaceStore.registerWorkspace({ id, urlKey, provider })` keeps ONE row per urlKey: one atomic upsert with `_id` = urlKey, as `workspace-halt` does (db-indexes.js:63-65). A re-bind (remove then re-add, or a new workspace id for the same key) updates `id`, `provider`, `updatedAt` and keeps `createdAt`. The row is exactly `{_id, id, urlKey, provider, createdAt, updatedAt}`, so a unique index on `urlKey` matches the data by construction. Returns `{ok: true, created, idChanged}` or `{ok: false, reason}`: `invalid-id`, `invalid-urlkey` (`validateWorkspaceUrlKey`, lib/workspace.js:1202, is case-insensitive; compare exactly), `invalid-provider` (linear, github, github-projects, jira, local). The store validates. `createWorkspace` is unchanged.
2. New `lib/workspace-registry.js`: `recordWorkspace(workspaceStore, workspace, { logger })`. Provider from `normalizeProvider` (lib/workspace.js:1054; active provider at last bind, informational). Hands the store only `{id, urlKey, provider}`, never mutates the workspace, catches every error (a synchronous throw too) and never changes the bind's result, redirect or session. Missing store or invalid input: one fixed line `[workspace-registry] skipped: <reason>`; a store error logs its class only. Callers await it, no timeout (same exposure as the edge write, lib/account-session.js:225).
3. Call it once at each of the 13 sites, straight after the ok check or refusal block, before `linkProvider` / `persistBinding`: lib/github-install-flow.js :845, :968, :1060; routes/auth.js :280, :423; routes/jira-auth.js :295, :629, :838, :927; routes/workspace.js:88 (before `localStore.seed`, :94). Three placements differ:
   * lib/pat-session.js:119: only inside the ok branch (:120-122 logs and carries on).
   * routes/held-connection.js:364: after the owner check (:369-375), before `providerAdded` (:377). That check undoes the bind; recording at :365 leaves a row for it.
   * routes/account-merge.js:150: inside `if (hasWorkspace)` (:136), after :150. `pending.workspace` holds tokens: it reaches nothing but `recordWorkspace`.
     Not sites: routes/email-auth.js:273, :593 (null workspace; email is an identity, never a provider), lib/account-store.js:266, held add-source (no edge), lib/owner-backfill.js, routes/test.js.
4. `workspaceStore` reaches each site as `resolveWorkspaceUrlKey` does, no default: server.js:1118 (PAT), :1474 (provider loop), :1485 (workspace), :1482 (merge; routes/account-merge.js:47 never got the resolver), :2556 (held). routes/github-auth.js:45-51 and github-projects-auth.js:53-59 forward a fixed list to lib/github-install-flow.js:179: add it to all three (a miss is a silent skip).
5. No reads move, nothing is deleted (removing a workspace leaves its row), and the plain `{urlKey: 1}` index (lib/db-indexes.js:454-459) stays.

## Tests

No live calls.

* workspace-store.test.js (MangoDB tmpdir): exact six fields; an object with `bindings`, `accessToken` and a run-time-built canary stores only the six; same key and id again keeps `createdAt`; key K with id A then id B leaves one row, `id` B, `createdAt` kept, `idChanged: true`; two concurrent first registers of one key give one `created: true`, no throw; each invalid reason.
* workspace-registry.test.js (new): a full workspace (canary built at run time, as dispatch-entrance-redaction-canary-sweep.test.js does) reaches a spy store as `deepEqual` `{id, urlKey, provider}`; a deep-frozen workspace is untouched; no throw when the store or the call throws; skip line; default provider; class, not message.
* All 13 sites: one table-driven test, not a per-file guard. Per row: success writes the row; refusal or conflict writes none; a throwing store leaves response, redirect and session unchanged. Arms in lin-3382-bind-arms.test.js (add `workspaceStore` to its world); PAT in pat-session.test.js (`freshStores()` :75; none if establish fails, session still saved); merge-confirm in account-identity.test.js (:164; none for a null-workspace merge). Conflict fixture: `findAccountByIdentity` returns another account while `session.accountId` is set (lin-3382-hop-class.test.js:51 returns null). Held: a non-owner edge writes none. The :190-197 flow (bind, remove, bind) ends with one row, second id. A last row fails on any non-test site missing from the table.
* lin-3382-hop-class.test.js: `workspaceStore` pins at each mount (server pins :260-271), merge included.

## Docs

lib/workspace-store.js header (:21-24) and the server.js:634-640 comment (write-only registry; keep their LIN-1328/1329/1330 references). source-map.md: entries for lib/workspace-store.js (none today) and lib/workspace-registry.js, beside :170-171; a short auth.md paragraph. CLAUDE.md is at its cap. No areas.json change (scripts/code-shape/areas.json:36 covers it): record base and head area-pair counts, expect 0 new. PR note: the dry-run's `URLKEY_SOURCES` lists `workspaces` (scripts/dry-run-urlkey-duplicates.mjs:80), empty today; its counts can shift.

## Out of scope

Reading the registry, any index, backfill or production run, deleting rows, routes/test.js seeds, kulcho.

## Open questions

Claim before the bind? Default: after, best effort (order matters only once step 3's index exists). Two ids binding one key (legacy Jira teammates, dry-run :32-33) flip the row's `id` to the last binder; step 2 finds it against holder evidence. A Linear rename makes a new row and leaves the old; a removed workspace's row keeps its dead id until the key is re-bound. No liveness marker: deferred. Note in the PR any site where "after success" is unclear.

## Operator notes

**Rules for this run**

* No live calls to outside services (GitHub, Linear, OpenRouter, [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>) or any other live host). Tests use the existing fakes.
* No paid model or OpenRouter calls.
* This is one PR. Don't split it into child tickets.
* No parallel forks or background sub-agents; one part at a time.
* Targeted tests while iterating (`node --test tests/unit/<file>.test.js`). Full unit suite (`npm run test:unit`) once before opening the PR. Leave e2e to CI.
* A failing-then-passing test is the witness for any behaviour change.
* Keep every existing ticket reference and every reason comment beside the code it governs; drop one only if its code is gone, and list those in the PR.
* A new production file (anything outside `tests/` and `docs/`) gets a pattern in `scripts/code-shape/areas.json` for the area that owns it, in the same PR. First match wins there, so check the file lands in that area and not in "Other features": run `node scripts/code-shape/seams.mjs . <commit>` at the base commit and at your final commit, report the area-pair count both times, and give the reason for any new pair. If it cannot run in your checkout (exit 2, `acorn` missing), record it as not run.
* Prompt text (templates, meta-prompt, runner prompt) is size-frozen (`tests/unit/prompt-size-budget.test.js`). If you add prompt text, remove bytes elsewhere or raise the ceiling with the reason recorded beside it (LIN-3633), and say which in the PR.
* Where a choice is still open, keep today's behaviour, write it up as an open question in the PR, and carry on. Never stop to wait for a person. A check that needs a live service or a person is recorded in the PR as not run (what, why, follow-up), not a reason to hold the close.

## Implemented

Merged as a6e0ae11 (PR [https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2000](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2000>), squash of e47323b8). The plan was implemented as approved; no sections of this description were pruned because it holds only the problem statement, Done-when list, tests and scope. Full history is in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
### Plan Review Verdict
**Verdict:** Approve — every claim I re-ran holds at `0eb4a2d1` (origin/main). Nothing blocking; four notes for the implementer below.

Grounded at `0eb4a2d1`. Read the description; the comment thread is empty.

**Staleness check.** Six commits touched cited files after the ticket was created: 0eb4a2d1, 331683f3, a9f81290, 3dfffe63, dca50589, d8c14f6d.
- Only the `server.js` line numbers are out of date. The current lines are: comment :641-647 (ticket :634-640), construction :649 (:642), PAT :1132 (:1118), provider loop :1488 (:1474), merge :1496 (:1482), workspace :1499 (:1485), held :2524-2536 (:2556).
- Every other cite checks out at HEAD:
  - All 13 site lines.
  - The held order: :364, then the owner check at :369-375, then `providerAdded` at :377.
  - `merge.js:136/150` and `pat-session.js:119-122`.
  - `db-indexes.js:63-65` and `:454-459`.
  - `workspace.js:1054` and `:1202`; `URL_KEY_REGEX` is `/i`.
  - `dry-run…:80`.
  - The forwarding lists at `github-auth.js:45-51`, `github-projects-auth.js:53-59` and `github-install-flow.js:179`.

**1. Completeness — pass.** I re-derived the class two ways:
- **Every caller that writes an account-to-workspace edge** (`bindAccountToWorkspace`). There are four: `account-session.js:225` (inside `establishAccount`), `account-store.js:266` (merge re-point, excluded), `account-merge.js:150` and `held-connection.js:364`.
- **Every production `establishAccount` call.** Eleven pass a workspace id: pat:119; gh:845, 968, 1060; auth:280, 423; jira:295, 629, 838, 927; workspace:88. Two pass `null`: email:274 and 594 (excluded). `routes/test.js` is excluded.

Together that is exactly the plan's 13 sites plus its named exclusions. As a cross-check I swept `upsertWorkspace` and every session-workspace push. Each lands on one of the 13 sites. `routes/provider-auth-routers.js` spreads `deps` in full, so the only fixed lists are the three files the plan already names.

**2. Strategy framing — pass.** The gap is named as LIN-3394 (step 1 of 3). This step fills it rather than routing around it.

**3. History — pass.** `git log -15` over the plan's files surfaces these constraints, and the plan already honours each one:
- LIN-3382: one resolver, no default.
- LIN-3334: record after the refusal blocks.
- LIN-3125 C2: held owner check and snapshot restore.
- LIN-1892 S3: null-workspace merge.
- LIN-675: no lib-to-routes imports; the new lib file needs none.

`workspace-store.js` has had only two commits; the plan follows the LIN-1337 atomic-upsert idiom from it.

**4. Session fit — no claim (non-blocking).** The plan gives no verdict and names no catches. The operator rule ("one PR, don't split") settles this, so I am not sending it back. Naming the catches would still help review: the five sites where the record runs before `linkProvider` (see 7), the conflict fixture, and the held owner check.

**5. Relaxation — pass.** Nothing is loosened. No test pins `workspaceStore` as inert (I searched `tests/`), so wiring it in flips no guard. The comment at server.js:641 must be rewritten, and the plan already covers that.

**6. Prerequisite refactor — pass.** There is no blocking subtask. The plumbing into each site is consumed directly by the call sites.

**7. Source of truth — pass, with one note.** `urlKey` and `id` come from the live workspace object, which is the primary source. `provider` comes from `normalizeProvider(workspace)`. At five sites the record runs before `linkProvider`: gh:845, gh:968, jira:295, jira:629, jira:838. `linkProvider` keeps `workspace.provider || provider`, so on an existing workspace the stored value is the same either way. The one exception is a legacy workspace with no provider set: before the link it reads `linear`, after it reads the newly linked kind. The field is informational, so this is not load-bearing. Say which one you chose in the PR.

**Non-blocking notes for implementation**
- **Erasure deletes registry rows.** 3dfffe63 (LIN-3423) landed after this ticket. `lib/account-erasure.js:151` lists `workspaces` as workspace-scoped by the `urlKey` field. A Full erasure of an Alone workspace will therefore delete its registry row.
  - This PR still deletes nothing, so Done-when 5 holds.
  - But "a removed workspace's row keeps its dead id until re-bound" now has one exception. Put it in the auth.md paragraph and the PR note, since steps 2 and 3 rely on the row contract.
- **areas.json.** The distilled brief says "add a pattern"; the description says "no change (:36 covers it)". The description is right: the first match for `lib/workspace-registry.js` is "Auth, accounts & workspaces" (regex `workspace-(?!kpi-stats\.js)[^/]*`). Record the seam pair counts at base and head as planned. In this checkout `seams.mjs` currently fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` because `node_modules` is missing. Run `npm install` first, or record it as not run.

Hand off to **implementation**. This Approve covers the plan only. It is not authorization to close the task.

### Implementation: PR open, CI green
**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2000 (commit e47323b8, branch feat/lin-3700-registry-urlkey-write)

- `WorkspaceStore.registerWorkspace` (one atomic upsert per urlKey, `_id` = urlKey, six fields, `createdAt` kept on re-bind) and new `lib/workspace-registry.js` `recordWorkspace` (best-effort, write-only, errors swallowed, class-only logging).
- Wired at all 13 sites with the three special placements (PAT inside ok branch; held-new after owner check; merge-confirm inside `hasWorkspace`). `workspaceStore` threaded explicitly, no default, including the three forwarding lists.
- Tests: table-driven over the real handlers (success writes the row, conflict writes none, throwing store changes nothing), plus a completeness guard. Full `npm run test:unit`: 18756 pass, 0 fail. Witness: with the production changes stashed, the new site/store tests fail; they pass with the change.
- CI: all jobs green (Unit tests, E2E 1-4, secret scan, CI success).
- Seams: area-pair links 67 at base and 67 at head (0 new); no areas.json change.

Open points recorded in the PR: five sites record before `linkProvider` (a legacy providerless workspace reads `linear`); Full erasure of an Alone workspace deletes its registry row (`lib/account-erasure.js:151`), noted in auth.md; I put the site table in a new test file rather than threading the store through `lin-3382-bind-arms.test.js`'s mounts. Merge is not mine; waiting on review.

## Review — LIN-3700

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2000 at head `e47323b8`. That is one commit on `0eb4a2d1`, which is still the tip of origin/main, so there has been no drift since the plan review.

CI: green on `e47323b8` (Unit tests, E2E 1–4, Secret scan, CI success; workflow `Tests`).

**Scope against the plan.** The diff covers the plan's surfaces and nothing more: 13 sites, `registerWorkspace`, the new `lib/workspace-registry.js`, server.js plus the three forwarding lists, and the docs. `createWorkspace` is unchanged. No `areas.json` change; the PR reports 67→67 seam pairs. No reads, indexes, backfill or deletes were added. All three special placements are right:
- **Held:** the record is after the owner-edge compensation block and before `providerAdded`.
- **PAT:** the record is only in the `else` of `!established.ok`.
- **Merge:** the record is inside `hasWorkspace`, after `bindAccountToWorkspace`.

There is one disclosed deviation: the site table lives in a new file (`lin-3700-registry-sites.test.js`) rather than in `lin-3382-bind-arms.test.js`. It drives the real handlers over real MangoDB stores, which is the level the ticket asked for, so I accept it.

**Regression check.** I ran `git log` over every touched file. The constraints that matter all still hold:
- LIN-3382: one resolver, no default.
- LIN-3334: record after the refusal blocks.
- LIN-3125 C2: held owner compensation.
- LIN-1892 S3: null-workspace merge.
- LIN-675: the new lib file imports only `lib/workspace.js`, no routes.

Nothing reverted is re-applied, and no ticket reference or reason comment was dropped. The LIN-1328/1329/1330 references are kept in both rewritten comments.

**Mutation checks (LIN-2274).** I reverted each mutation afterwards, and the tree is clean. All 10 went red:
1. Dropped the record at jira live-container (`existing`) → 2 site tests fail, plus the completeness guard.
2. Moved the held record before the owner check → "a non-owner edge records nothing" fails.
3. Made the PAT record unconditional → "a failed establish records nothing" fails.
4. Put `createdAt` in `$set` instead of `$setOnInsert` → 3 fail (store and re-bind flow).
5. Removed the try/catch in `recordWorkspace` → 14 fail (throwing-store rows, sync throw).
6. Spread the whole workspace into `registerWorkspace` → 2 fail (deepEqual hand-off, merge spy).
7. Dropped the 11000 retry → the fake-collection retry test fails. MangoDB itself does not race, so only the fake witnesses this.
8. Moved the auth.js add-source record above the conflict block → the conflict test fails.
9. Dropped `workspaceStore` from the github-auth forwarding list → 4 fail (site rows and hop pin).
10. Dropped `workspaceStore` from the server.js merge mount → the hop-class pin fails.

**Class check.** The bind-site class is closed by the completeness guard: every production `establishAccount` and `bindAccountToWorkspace` caller must have a matching `recordWorkspace`, with the named exclusions. I also looked at the readers of the `workspaces` collection, which now holds rows for the first time:
- `scripts/dry-run-urlkey-duplicates.mjs:80`: already noted in the PR.
- `lib/account-erasure.js:151`: Full erasure deletes the row. Documented in auth.md and the PR.
- `scripts/scan-same-kind-sources-lin3332.mjs:109`: registry rows have no `bindings`, so they flag nothing, but `scannedWorkspaces` now counts them as "durable workspace docs". Harmless, and not in the PR note.

Otherwise the change is isolated.

**Non-blocking notes**
- The throwing-store `observe()` compares status, redirect, the session's workspace *count* and `accountSet`, not the full session or response body. That is weaker than "session unchanged", but mutation 5 shows it still bites.
- A refusal other than a conflict (for example the workspace-limit 400) is not driven per site. The conflict block sits after those refusals, so mutation 8 covers the ordering.
- For LIN-3702/LIN-1330, outside this ticket: registry rows (`_id` = urlKey) and `createWorkspace` rows (`_id` = workspace id) share one collection. Once LIN-1330 wires `createWorkspace`, a unique `{urlKey:1}` index would see two documents per key. Steps 2 and 3 should decide that before building the index.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Real MongoDB return shape (inside: a claim the store's `created`/`idChanged` depends on).** CI runs MangoDB only. On the mongodb 7.0.0 driver in `package.json`, `findOneAndUpdate(..., {upsert:true, returnDocument:'before'})` returns the prior document or `null`, not a `ModifyResult`. That matches the codebase idiom (`free-tier-store.js:164`). *Settle after the deploy:* after the first real bind, check that `db.workspaces.findOne({_id: <that urlKey>})` returns exactly the six fields with `createdAt == updatedAt`. Nothing in the bind path reads `created`/`idChanged`, so a wrong shape could not break a bind.
- **Real provider entry paths write the row (inside: the ticket's goal, "production has rows under each key").** The 13 sites run with fake providers and stores; no real Linear, GitHub or Jira OAuth runs in CI. *Settle after the deploy:* after one real sign-in or bind per provider in use, `db.workspaces.countDocuments({_id: '<key>'})` is 1 for that key. *Monitor:* the fixed log lines `[workspace-registry] skipped: <reason>` and `[workspace-registry] store error: <Class>`. Any of them in production means a site is skipping silently. Only live traffic can exercise the real OAuth callbacks.
- **Rollback (inside).** Revert the single squash commit for this PR (head `e47323b8`). Rows already written stay behind, but nothing reads them, so a revert restores the old behaviour. They are not a migration.
- **`scan-same-kind-sources-lin3332.mjs` now counts registry rows (outside: a different script's reporting).** No correctness impact. Close-out can add one line beside the existing dry-run note in the PR body. No ticket is needed.
- **Erasure deletes an Alone workspace's row (outside: LIN-3423 behaviour).** Discharged: documented in auth.md and the PR for steps 2 and 3.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

The implementation matches every Done-when item and all three special placements. All 10 mutations of the load-bearing paths went red, and CI is green on `e47323b8`. What remains is the post-deploy live check, the named monitor, and one PR-note line. Next: **close-out**.

## Close-out — LIN-3700

**Merged:** PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2000, squash commit `a6e0ae11`, pinned with `--match-head-commit e47323b8`. Base `main` was still `0eb4a2d1`, so no conflict.

**CI:** green on the exact merged head `e47323b8` (Unit tests, E2E 1-4, Secret scan, CI success; workflow `Tests`). Read fresh just before the merge, and again after I edited the PR body (head unchanged).

**Changes I made after approval:** no code changes; review asked for none. I only edited the PR body to add the close-out notes the review asked for: the `scan-same-kind-sources-lin3332.mjs` line, the rollback, and the post-deploy checks.

**Ledger**
- *Real MongoDB return shape (inside):* not run. It needs the production database, which I have no access to, and the deployed commit is not something I confirmed in this session. Recorded in the PR. Check: after the first real bind, `db.workspaces.findOne({_id: <urlKey>})` has exactly the six fields with `createdAt == updatedAt`. Nothing in the bind path reads `created` or `idChanged`, so a wrong shape cannot break a bind. Who can run it: the operator with production DB access.
- *Real provider entry paths (inside):* not run, for the same reason (needs live OAuth and production DB). Check: after one real sign-in or bind per provider in use, `db.workspaces.countDocuments({_id: '<key>'})` is 1. Named monitor, as review wrote it: the log lines `[workspace-registry] skipped: <reason>` and `[workspace-registry] store error: <Class>`; either one in production means a site is skipping.
- *Rollback (inside):* revert the single squash commit `a6e0ae11`. Rows already written stay behind and nothing reads them.
- *`scan-same-kind-sources-lin3332.mjs` counts registry rows (outside):* no correctness impact; recorded as a line in the PR body, no ticket needed, as review said.
- *Erasure deletes an Alone workspace's row (outside):* already documented in auth.md and the PR; also carried onto LIN-3702 for steps 2 and 3.

**Follow-ups:** one outside item from review's non-blocking notes: registry rows and `createWorkspace` rows would share the `workspaces` collection, so a unique `{urlKey: 1}` index could see two documents per key once LIN-1330 wires `createWorkspace`. This is for the index step, so I put it as a comment on LIN-3702 (it already exists and covers it) instead of filing a new ticket.

**Description:** snapshot taken and verified in `/snapshots` before editing. Nothing was pruned: the description holds only the problem statement, Done-when list, tests, scope and operator notes. I appended a short Implemented stub with the PR link.

**Related tickets:** LIN-3701 and LIN-3702 are the next steps and stay open; LIN-3705 and LIN-3696 are unrelated.
